title: D-Link DIR-X1860Z Flaws Enable Unauthenticated Admin Password Reset and Wi-Fi Credential Theft
content_md: D-Link has patched two local-network vulnerabilities in its non-US DIR-X1860Z router that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to replace the administrator password and recover Wi-Fi configuration data, including wireless credentials . The issues affect hardware revision A1/V1.0 running firmware V1.0.2.220120.165402 and stem from insufficient authentication controls in the device’s OpenWrt-based ubus JSON-RPC management interface. The primary vulnerability involves the routerd.passwd_set method exposed through the router’s ubus JSON-RPC interface. D-Link DIR-X1860Z Flaws According to D-Link, an attacker connected to the same local network could invoke the privileged method without proper authentication and establish a new administrator password. After changing the password, the attacker could log in through the router’s standard administration workflow and obtain an authenticated administrative ubus_rpc_session . This access could give the intruder control over router settings, enabling further network manipulation such as changing DNS settings , modifying firewall rules, altering port-forwarding configurations, or locking legitimate owners out of their devices. The affected management service is accessible through TCP port 23355 at the /ubus endpoint.
